SMTO-EXE-0092 — The screenshot or image is too big for SMTO

GUID: 26fbde73-b37d-5431-94d1-a46d3b60de2b
Slug: screen-size-limit
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • The screen area or image SMTO was asked to use is larger than SMTO allows, and SMTO never shrinks pictures on its own. It stopped, so nothing was captured or read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to capture one window or a smaller area instead of a whole very large or high-resolution screen. Each picture can be at most 16 million pixels, and SMTO won't shrink a larger one.
  2. If you gave SMTO an image file, use a PNG or JPEG under 16 MB, for example by cropping it or saving it at a lower resolution. Files over 16 MB or 16 million pixels are refused before SMTO opens them.
  3. If the computer has more than 32 screens connected, disconnect the ones you don't need, then ask again. SMTO lists at most 32 screens and stops if there are more.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the screenshot or the text you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the size of the screen or image you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the screenshot or its contents into the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Screen processing exceeded a resource limit (more than 32 displays, more than 16,000,000 pixels or 16 MiB encoded) or received non-positive or non-integer image dimensions.

What this means

  • Screen processing exceeded the display-count, encoded-byte or pixel bound, or rejected invalid nonpositive/noninteger dimensions. No automatic image shrinking resolves the request. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Screen processing exceeded the display-count, encoded-byte or pixel bound, or rejected invalid nonpositive/noninteger dimensions. No automatic image shrinking resolves the request.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the failed bound concerns display enumeration, image bytes or dimensions; preserve the intended observed area when reducing scope.

How to fix it

  • check_pixels, BoundedBuffer and decode_image enforce PIXEL_LIMIT 16,000,000 and BYTE_LIMIT 16 MiB (and DISPLAY_LIMIT 32 during Linux enumeration); dimensions must be positive integers. Request a smaller region or supply a smaller PNG/JPEG; there is no automatic downscaling. If display count is the failure, inspect enumeration separately.
  • Check the reported bound. Use a valid smaller region or bounded image when the image is too large; inspect display enumeration separately if its count is the failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select a smaller rectangle or local PNG/JPEG. Images are limited to 16 million pixels and 16 MiB encoded bytes; no automatic downscaling occurs.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid explicit region/image fits the current limits without silent downscaling or truncation.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
